title: Build an interactive greeter
idea: Put it together: ask, decide, and reply with a personalized f-string message. Learner assembles a full small interactive program.

exercises.prompt: Task: ask for a name, then if the name is "admin" greet with special access, else a normal welcome, using the name in the message. What are the pieces?
options: input() to ask, if/else to decide, an f-string to reply with the name
exercises.explanation: Ask, decide, reply - the full interactive pattern, with an f-string to personalize the message.

exercises.prompt: Which line asks for the name and stores it?
exercises.explanation: input() shows the prompt and returns the typed text into name.
Ask, branch on the name, and reply - the else uses an f-string to drop the name into the greeting.

exercises.prompt:
Fill the marker so {name} is replaced by its value:

print(____"Hello, {name}!")
exercises.explanation: The f makes it an f-string, so {name} shows the typed name. (f-string review, now with live input.)

exercises.prompt: The user types admin. What prints?
exercises.explanation: "admin" matches the if, so the special branch prints "Welcome, boss!".

exercises.prompt: The user types Ada. What prints?
exercises.explanation: "Ada" is not "admin", so the else runs and the f-string fills in the name: "Hello, Ada!".

exercises.prompt: The user types Admin (capital A). What prints?
options: Hello, Admin! - because "Admin" does not equal "admin"
exercises.explanation: Case matters: "Admin" fails the == "admin" test, so it falls to the friendly else. A real capitalization gotcha.

exercises.prompt: The greeter behaves differently for different typed names, proving input() drives the output.
exercises.explanation: Yes - "admin" gets one message, other names get another. The user's answer shapes the result.

exercises.prompt: To check this program works, which inputs should you try?
options: "admin" (hits the if) and a normal name like "Ada" (hits the else)
exercises.explanation: Test one input per branch. Covering both the if and else proves the whole decision.

options: A complete ask-decide-reply program using input(), if/else, and an f-string
exercises.explanation: That is a real interactive program - the full decision toolkit reacting to a typed answer.
